findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "crypto-security" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: crypto-security_intent-safety · Private data: contact_us · Public sink: crypto-security_transaction-intent-verify, crypto-security_intent-safety, crypto-security_proxy-upgrade-storage-audit, crypto-security_storage-slot-grade, contact_us.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: crypto-security_intent-safety · Private data: contact_us · Public sink: crypto-security_transaction-intent-verify, crypto-security_intent-safety, crypto-security_proxy-upgrade-storage-audit, crypto-security_storage-slot-grade, contact_us

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "crypto-security_transaction-intent-verify" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Compare an EVM transaction's calldata and native value with the action declared in the request. Docs: https://www.brainiac.software/api/crypto-security/transaction-intent-verify Keywords: before you sign or send a transaction, chainId, contractAddress, calldata, value, expectedAction, expected, abi,"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
